stories.body: The S&P 500 fell 265.44 points, or 3.70%, to 6,910.39 for a seventh straight loss and an 8.6% weekly drop, its worst week since April 2025; the Nasdaq Composite lost 5.28% to 22,617.73 and the Dow 1.93% to 48,147.33, Capp Notes reported. Yahoo Finance said both the S&P 500 and the Dow closed in correction. SPY closed −3.64% at $689.81 and QQQ −5.67% at $608.45 (us-market-data).
stories.title: S&P 500 sinks 3.7% to 6,910 and enters correction as the Nasdaq drops 5.3% and turns negative for 2026
stories.why: Friday's 4:00 PM candle is the last completed close of the week; Monday's first hourly close decides how much of the drop carries, never a weekend or after-hours print.

stories.body: Communication services fell 2.66% and consumer discretionary 2.95%, Capp Notes reported, while Yahoo Finance said Microsoft and Amazon were down about 6% for the week. Friday closes: Meta −5.93% at $560.84, Tesla −7.64% at $345.82, Amazon −4.10%, Microsoft −2.77%, Alphabet −2.59%, Apple −1.90% (us-market-data).
stories.title: Meta −5.93% and Tesla −7.64% lead megacap losses; Amazon −4.10%, Microsoft −2.77%
stories.why: Every megacap closed below Thursday; each is still judged on its own completed hourly closes against its daily MA20, not on the group's drop.

stories.body: Technology fell 7.27%, by far the worst S&P 500 sector, and the Nasdaq-100 dropped 5.61% after touching bear-market territory intraday, Capp Notes reported, as memory and storage stocks sank. Closes: Micron −13.89% at $594.51, AMD −13.25% at $424.39, Broadcom −12.19%, Intel −7.97% (us-market-data).
stories.title: Micron −13.89%, AMD −13.25% and Broadcom −12.19% as technology sinks 7.3%
stories.why: Closes this far below the hourly MAs leave wide gaps to every average; any reclaim is read only on completed hourly closes.

stories.body: Financials fell 1.82% and energy 0.62%, Capp Notes reported, as WTI crude settled 0.93% higher at $83.98. Closes: JPMorgan −3.03% at $310.53, Bank of America −3.15%, Exxon +0.67% at $159.99, Chevron +0.91% at $208.37 (us-market-data).
stories.title: Banks fall about 3% while Exxon +0.67% and Chevron +0.91% close higher as oil settles up
stories.why: Exxon and Chevron closed above Thursday while banks fell with the index; relative moves are context for each symbol's own hourly structure.

stories.body: Nvidia closed −14.01% at $125.53, Capp Notes reported, after Reuters said SEC enforcement staff are examining potential accounting issues and California Attorney General Rob Bonta sent an investigative subpoena late Thursday over whether its chips reached China. CNBC said the stock ended its seventh straight weekly loss, the longest since the 2008 financial crisis.
stories.title: Nvidia plunges 14% to $125.53, its worst day since January 2025, amid reported SEC accounting review
stories.why: A 14% close below Thursday leaves Nvidia far under every hourly MA; structure is rebuilt only from completed hourly closes, not from headlines.

stories.body: Gold futures fell 4.63% to about $3,515 and silver futures 7.41% to about $41.03, Capp Notes reported, while the dollar index eased 0.07% to about 103.84 from Thursday's 19-month high. GLD closed −3.67% at $322.87 and SLV −6.74% at $36.97.
stories.title: Gold futures fall 4.6% to about $3,515, a 14.5-month low; silver drops 7.4%
stories.why: GLD and SLV fell with stocks rather than against them; their hourly closes, not the futures prints, are what the structure rules read.

stories.body: WTI crude settled 0.93% higher at $83.98 and Brent 0.64% higher at $92.57, though oil fell for a third straight week, Capp Notes and EnergyNow reported. Capp Notes said the Houthis threatened Saudi ports, Iranian attacks on Hormuz tankers have run at about one a day in November, per UOB, and Russia launched more than 400 drones and over 110 missiles at Ukraine. USO closed +1.12% and OXY +0.17%.
stories.title: Oil settles higher on Middle East tensions but posts a third weekly loss; Russia launches 400+ drones at Ukraine
stories.why: December WTI expired Friday, so USO's next hourly closes track the January contract; supply headlines can gap it at Monday's open.

stories.body: The VIX rose 26.20% to 35.89, its highest close since late March, Capp Notes reported. Yahoo Finance said the index briefly spiked to 40 during the session, about twice its 2026 average of 18.4.
stories.title: VIX jumps 26% to 35.89, its highest close since late March
stories.why: A VIX near 36 into the weekend widens option premiums and spreads; contract counts and liquidity are read at chain time on Monday, not assumed from Friday.

stories.body: The 10-year yield fell 12 bp to 4.92% and the 2-year 13 bp to 4.63%, Capp Notes reported. Governor Lisa Cook warned that waiting to raise rates risks getting behind the curve, and Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson said she would be open to back-to-back hikes; Kalshi priced a 25 bp hike at the Dec. 9 meeting at 90%.
stories.title: 10-year yield falls 12 bp to 4.92%, its biggest drop since Oct. 22, as Fed officials talk up hikes
stories.why: Yields fell sharply while stocks slid, a flight to safety rather than rate pressure; that is context next to, never instead of, the hourly closes.

stories.body: Taiwan's Taiex fell 6.23% to 36,033.29 for a record 17.5% weekly loss, the Nikkei 225 5.06% and the Kospi 5.21%, while India's Sensex rose 1.08%, Capp Notes reported. In Europe the STOXX 600 fell 2.00%, the CAC 40 1.89% and the FTSE 100 1.02%; the DAX closed 2.45% lower (Trading Economics).
stories.title: Taiex posts a record 17.5% weekly loss as Asia and Europe close sharply lower
stories.why: Japan's markets are closed Monday, so Seoul and Taipei carry the first overseas read on chips before the US open.

stories.body: The University of Michigan's final November sentiment index rose to 51.5, in line with estimates, and one-year inflation expectations fell to 3.7%, the lowest since March, from 4.3% at mid-month, Capp Notes reported. AP said consumers cited easing gas prices and improved business expectations.
stories.title: Consumer sentiment rises to 51.5 as one-year inflation expectations fall to 3.7%
stories.why: The 10:00 AM release landed as the first hourly candle closed; the data did not stop the slide in the later closes.

stories.body: It was the third Friday of the month, so monthly stock options expired at the close and the December WTI contract also expired, Options Oracle and 24/7 Wall St. reported; options on Anthropic start trading Monday, Options Oracle said. Anthropic fell 8.50% to $88.91 in its first full session, Capp Notes reported.
stories.title: Monthly options expired at Friday's close as the VIX hit its highest close since March
stories.why: The November monthly series is gone; 7–21 DTE entries from Monday use the weekly and December expiries.

stories.body: Monday brings the Chicago Fed index at 8:30 AM, S&P Global flash PMIs at 9:45 AM, a 2-year note auction at 1:00 PM and NY Fed President John Williams at 4:00 PM, with HPE, Zoom and Agilent reporting after the close; Japan's markets are closed, Capp Notes said. Schwab lists October PCE prices, durable goods and the second estimate of Q3 GDP on Wednesday; US markets close Thursday for Thanksgiving, and Friday stocks close at 1:00 PM ET and bonds at 2:00 PM.
stories.title: Thanksgiving week: flash PMIs Monday, PCE and GDP Wednesday, markets shut Thursday and close early Friday
stories.why: A four-session week with an early close Friday: under the early-close rule C4 is the last hourly close that day.

tone.text: Friday closed in a broad AI-led rout: the S&P 500 fell for a seventh straight session into correction and lost 8.6% on the week, technology sank 7.27% and the VIX closed at 35.89, its highest since late March, Capp Notes reported; consumer staples was the only sector higher.
